source.title: Generalization in Neural Networks Through the Lens of Magnitude Potential
source.authors: Sahel Torkamani; Henry Gouk; Rik Sarkar

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures train/validation accuracy on modular-addition grokking experiments and uses a new geometric measure to track their training dynamics. It reports results bearing on delayed generalization and progress signals, but does not test the specific mechanistic circuit claims or the training-set-size relationship.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports CIFAR memorization correlations, 2D decision-boundary changes, and neural-collapse comparisons; these do not test the listed claim versions. Results about training-set-size dependence, Fourier circuits, and removal of memorizing components are not reported as experiments.
record.test_reason: The paper uses standard modular-addition grokking setups as a testbed for its own geometric indicator, the magnitude-potential (MP) ratio. It reports how well that indicator tracks the transition. It does not measure the size of the delay, vary training-set size, or probe the generalizing mechanism. The accuracy curves show delayed generalization in the chosen setups, but they are context for the method, not a test of any version. The MP ratio is a logit-space geometric score, not a measure of circuit formation, so it does not bear on V2 as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that the aggregated MP ratio is a leading geometric indicator of grokking that needs no architecture or loss assumptions: the training MP-ratio rise precedes the validation-accuracy transition, and its standard deviations fall and its means stabilize near 100% validation accuracy. They note that the weight norm gives a slightly earlier signal. Grokking is only one of several applications; the others are memorization correlation on CIFAR-100, decision-boundary changes, and robustness to neural collapse.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular-addition tasks and train/validation accuracy to examine grokking, with an MP-ratio measure added. The MLP experiment uses modulo 37, a 70/30 split, MSE, and SGD; an additional Transformer experiment uses modulo 113, a 30/70 split, cross-entropy, and AdamW. No training-set-size sweep is reported.
record.method_sensitivity: MP-ratio scale t is varied; the paper says qualitatively similar trajectories occur across tested t values. The grokking experiments also use different models, tasks, data splits, and optimizers.

fits_no_version.finding: In the mod-37 MLP, the mean training MP ratio (a logit-space geometric score) begins rising, and its across-sample standard deviation falls, before validation accuracy rises. The validation MP ratio rises together with the accuracy rise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Logit-space class-geometry measures (such as the MP ratio) give a leading signal of the grokking transition in modular arithmetic.

fits_no_version.finding: The weight norm keeps decreasing and gives a slightly earlier signal than the MP ratio. Training and validation losses decline gradually with no discontinuities, and all signals stabilize together near 100% validation accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-norm decline precedes the accuracy jump in grokking (a continuous progress signal). This is relevant to V2/V5 but is not a mechanistic test.

record.problems: The modular-addition grokking evidence is limited to small experimental setups and one split per task; the paper notes that large, overparameterized models remain unverified. No independent-run uncertainty is reported for these grokking results, and several plotted values are not stated numerically. The training-set-size dependence in V1 is not tested.

untested.parts: How the delay scales with training-set size; the delay length is not quantified. Only one split per task is used, with one run each.
Formation of a Fourier or other generalizing circuit, later removal of memorizing components, and mechanistic progress measures.
Grokking on non-algorithmic data, and switching it on or off via initialization scale or weight norm. The CIFAR experiments are not grokking experiments.
LLM pretraining or fine-tuning is not studied.
No weight-decay comparison, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
No comparison of the algorithms learned across runs.
Optimizer and floating-point artifacts are not controlled or tested.

missing.what: The weight norm decreases slightly before the MP-ratio signal and the accuracy rise, and losses decrease gradually without discontinuity, in the mod-37 MLP grokking run.

record.verdict_notes: The grokking runs are standard testbeds. The Transformer run copies the Nanda et al. setup from an original source. Each has one run and one split, and no delay or dataset-size measurements are reported. The reader's V1 and V2 'supports' labels are dropped: V1 is only reproduced as context, and the MP ratio is not the V2 circuit mechanism.

versions.untested_parts: The effect of training-set size on delay is not varied or tested; the paper reports one split for each modular-addition experiment.
The paper measures MP-ratio progress signals but does not identify a Fourier algorithm or test gradual formation of a generalizing circuit or later removal of memorizing components.
Non-algorithmic grokking and switching it through initialization scale or weight norm are not tested.
LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is not studied.
The paper does not compare weight-decay conditions, test an efficiency account, or measure a critical dataset size or ungrokking.
The paper does not compare identifiable algorithms across runs.
Optimizer instability and floating-point/softmax artifact explanations are not tested.

relation.reason: The study uses established grokking dynamics to demonstrate its geometric measurement method; accuracy curves provide context for evaluating that method.

tranche.reason: Standard modular-addition grokking runs serve as testbeds for the proposed MP-ratio indicator. The study evaluates that indicator's timing and stabilization signals without independently testing the claim versions' mechanisms, dataset-size dependence, or regime dependence.

source_check.notes: The abbreviated conditions are accurate but omit MLP MSE loss and SGD weight decay 1e-4, and Transformer cross-entropy loss and AdamW weight decay 1.0. Accuracy results are qualitative or figure-only; no numerical delay or training-set-size sweep is reported.
